1.title: Heaven and earth open, and good bonds come together
1.plain: When heaven and earth open, good bonds are tied. The day is good, the hour is good, and everything is in place. Drawing this lot is no small thing, but its last line sets a condition: walk upright and stand straight, and those above will notice you and call for you. The whole poem says that timing and connection have arrived, and if you act with integrity, you can receive the good that comes.
1.overall: This lot means a very good start, with timing and connection on your side. It stresses one thing, being upright. When you act in the open and take no shortcuts, the chance to be seen and promoted comes to you. Now is a good time to move forward with confidence. Do what needs doing, do it properly, and don't be afraid.
1.love: If you're in a flirtation, the bond is already tied, so be sincere and say where you stand. Don't play testing games. If you've lost contact, a good moment is opening. Send an honest message without heavy emotion. It helps more than guessing. If you're hoping to get back together, talk plainly about the original problem, and the other person will be more willing to return. If you're in a relationship, this is a good time to talk about long-term plans, and the bond will grow steadier.
1.work: If you're job hunting or thinking of changing jobs, an opening is in front of you. Present your résumé and interviews honestly, without over-polishing. A manager or senior colleague may be watching, and upright work will be remembered. If you're negotiating a deal, state your terms clearly and follow the rules. The more upright you are, the smoother it goes.

1.ji: Taking shortcuts to gain an edge

2.title: The whale is still in the rivers, waiting to leap the Dragon Gate
2.plain: The whale hasn't transformed yet, so it can only stay in the rivers and lakes. It isn't yet allowed to rise and leave these waters. One day its form will change completely and it will carry itself with great presence. Then it can leap over the Dragon Gate, the legendary threshold where a fish becomes a dragon. The whole poem says you have great ability, but it isn't yet time to jump.
2.overall: This lot says "not yet." Your ability is considerable, but the time hasn't come, and rushing now is likely to waste effort. For now, hold your position and build a thick foundation while you wait to truly change. The day of the leap will come, but not by hurrying. Stay calm and do your homework.
2.love: If you're in a flirtation, the feeling is still brewing. Don't push for an answer yet. Let time together build naturally. If you've lost contact, the other person won't swim over for now. Living your own life well helps more than sending message after message. If you're hoping to get back together, talking now will mostly go nowhere, so wait until both of you have changed. If you're in a relationship, it's still in a growing stage. Compare less, be present more, and it will slowly rise.
2.work: If you're job hunting or thinking of changing jobs, opportunities may be thinner than you expected for now. Build skills and a portfolio first, and don't apply at random. If you're hoping to switch jobs or get promoted, the timing isn't ripe, so stay put and train your strength. If you're negotiating a deal, watch first and don't rush to sign.
2.ask_next: You're still waiting for the leap. What do you most want to know: roughly when your turn will come?
2.ji: Rushing before the time has come

3.title: The swallow carries mud, and the nest collapses again
3.plain: Into the wind and through the rain, out and back again, always toiling and running about, like a swallow. It carries mud home with great effort and layers it into a nest, but in the end the nest breaks and turns back into a heap of mud. The whole poem says you work hard, but your method or direction is off, and what you build won't hold. Stop first and look for where it leaks.
3.overall: This lot doesn't say you aren't trying hard enough. It reminds you that effort in the wrong place is wasted. Don't rush to do more right now. Look back and check why what you've done doesn't last: is the base unsteady, the direction wrong, or are you leaning too much on others? Repair the foundation first, then put in your effort, and your hard work will count.
3.love: If you're in a flirtation and you keep giving while the other person doesn't catch it, pause and ask whether you're the only one building. If you've lost contact and keep reaching out only to fall silent again, the problem isn't solved, so think it through before you message. If you're hoping to get back together, using the same old way of relating means that even a repair can break again. If you're in a relationship, don't just stay busy. Tend the foundation of the relationship together.
3.work: At work it's easy to stay busy for hours with nothing to show, so sort out your process and find why you keep starting over. If you're job hunting, rather than sending out many applications at random, fix your résumé and then apply with focus. If you're negotiating a deal, see clearly whether the other side can hold up, so it doesn't fall apart halfway.
3.ask_next: Mend the foundation first. What do you most want to know: which days suit a fresh start?

4.title: The broken mirror made whole, a second chance arrives
4.plain: The shattered flower mirror joins together and becomes round again. Man or woman, you can find a partner anew and begin a marriage or relationship again. From this time, the look of the home changes completely, and later more blessings and good fortune are added, with care for the next generation too. The whole poem says that what was broken can be reconnected, or a new beginning can be made, and your days will keep getting better.
4.overall: This lot is about starting over. What was once shattered or severed now has a chance to be mended, or to be replaced with a fresh situation. Don't be bound by past failures. A second chance is just as worth holding on to. Now is a good time to put down your burdens, tidy your surroundings, and meet the coming change with a fresh mind.
4.love: If you're in a flirtation and you've been hurt before, you can relax a little this time and give a new person a chance. If you've lost contact, the connection may be able to rejoin, so try a greeting first to feel the warmth. If you're hoping to get back together, this lot is kind to you, but be sure to talk through why you parted last time. If you're in a relationship, it's a good time to change rhythm together, such as moving or planning your future.
4.work: If you're changing jobs or careers, starting over is a good choice, and there's no shame in turning back or taking a bend. A deal that once fell through can be approached again. If you're job hunting, former colleagues and old contacts are worth reaching out to again.
4.ask_next: A second chance is right in front of you. What do you most want to know: which days suit speaking up again?
4.yi: Put down burdens and start over

5.title: One swing of the hoe, and spring water and a true friend both come
5.plain: Pick up a hoe and dig, hoping to find spring water. If you're willing to put in the effort, you'll be the first to get it. Unexpectedly, you meet a true friend who understands you. The two of you join hands at first meeting and fly up together to the blue sky. The whole poem says that if you act first, results will come, and along the way you'll meet someone willing to give you a lift.
5.overall: The point of this lot is to act first. Spring water doesn't appear by itself. You have to dig, and those willing to work get it first. Better still, in the process you'll meet someone you click with, who speeds things upward. Now is a good time to take the initiative, while watching for new partners who appear around you.
5.love: If you're in a flirtation, taking the initiative will get a response, and whoever speaks first more easily gets an answer. If you've lost contact, you can message first, and the other person may not refuse. If you're single, a true friend may appear at an unexpected place, so go out more and join activities. If you're hoping to get back together, effort helps, but listen sincerely to what the other person thinks. If you're in a relationship, working together toward a goal will bring you closer.
5.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, be active in sending résumés and booking interviews, because the earlier you move, the better. At work you may meet a manager who appreciates you or a good partner, so seize the chance to work together. If you're starting a business or negotiating a deal, finding the right person means rising together.
5.ask_next: Spring water comes only if you dig. What do you most want to know: which days are most rewarding to start?
5.yi: Pick up the hoe and start working
5.ji: Sitting and waiting for chances to come

6.title: Giving yourself up is too hard, so look after yourself first
6.plain: The first line paints an extreme picture: throwing yourself down a cliff to feed a tiger. The poem goes on to say that only a truly great person could do this, that giving oneself up entirely is hard to meet again, and that you could search the whole world and not find such a person. The whole poem says that complete self-sacrifice is rare, so don't demand it of yourself, and don't expect others to do it for you.
6.overall: This lot reminds you to see the limits of giving. You may be pushing yourself for something or someone until there's little of you left, or you may be expecting someone to sacrifice everything for you. Neither lasts. Now is a good time to put your energy where it's doable and sustainable. Take responsibility, but don't pour all of yourself in.
6.love: If you're in a flirtation, you can express your liking, but don't keep giving in or put yourself too low. If you've lost contact, you don't need to wrong yourself to win contact back. If you're hoping to get back together and the terms are that you give way on everything, think about whether it's worth it. If you're in a relationship, don't expect the other person to give everything for you. Leave each other some room, and the relationship will be healthier.
6.work: Being responsible at work is good, but don't take all the responsibility onto yourself. If you're job hunting or changing jobs, look after your own interests when discussing terms. If you're negotiating a deal, don't let one side sacrifice too much. Divide the work clearly so it can last.
6.ask_next: Giving needs boundaries. What would you most like to know: which days are good for saying things plainly?
6.yi: Give within what you can do

7.title: Crossing mountains and rivers, too far to return
7.plain: The road is exhausting, with one danger after another. You drag mud and water and still have mountains to cross. What's more worrying is the thought of running off to find another way out, only to end up thousands of miles away with no way back. The whole poem says: things are hard right now, but rushing off to somewhere new may be even harder to clean up. Don't run off yet.
7.overall: This lot says the hardship in front of you is real. It also warns that trying to solve things by changing places may take you further and leave you more tired. Don't rush into a big change now. Break the difficulty into small pieces and handle them one at a time. If you really do leave, think through a way back first, and don't burn the bridge.
7.love: If you're in a flirtation, the other person has been hot and cold lately, so don't dive in headfirst. If you've lost contact, don't do anything too impulsive to win them back, like suddenly showing up at their door. If you're hoping to get back together, there are quite a few practical problems in the way, so sort out your own state first. If you're in a relationship, especially long-distance or living apart, put in more effort to stay in touch so you don't drift further apart.
7.work: If you're thinking of changing jobs or taking an overseas posting, find out the conditions clearly first and don't leave on impulse. Job hunting may be harder than you expected, so keep a way back open. A deal may drag on and get messy, so settle the details before you commit.
7.ask_next: Don't rush to go far away. What would you most like to know: when is a better time to set out?
7.yi: Break the problem in front of you into small pieces

8.title: Pine and cypress in winter cold, unbowed by wind and frost
8.plain: The pine and cypress in the cold winter were planted long ago and raised slowly. Rain, snow, wind and frost cannot bring them down. One day they will be put to great use. In a career, they become the beams that hold up the house. The whole poem says: you can withstand the test, the hardship now is helping you grow, and later you will be given responsibility.
8.overall: This lot means: if you can endure, you will become timber. You may feel worn down and the surroundings cold, but that is proof you can hold on. Don't rush to see results right away, because pines grow slowly. Keep putting down roots and working steadily, and this foundation will later let you carry big responsibilities.
8.love: If you're in a flirtation, feelings need time to grow, so don't give up over a moment of coldness. If you've lost contact, real connection can survive distance, so take care of yourself first and send a message when the time comes. If you're hoping to get back together and you've both matured, this relationship has a chance to be steadier. If you're in a relationship, you've been through storms, and now is the time to sink your roots deeper together.
8.work: At work you are being tempered, and this experience will become your capital. If you're job hunting or changing jobs, a position with long-term prospects matters more than short-term high pay. There is a chance you'll be given responsibility, but it takes time to build up.
8.ask_next: Growing slowly into a pillar. What would you most like to know: which days suit going after a chance to show your work?
8.yi: Keep rooting steadily and keep going
8.ji: Rushing to see results right away

9.title: Say what's on your mind, and your heart is a clear mirror
9.plain: Thank you for coming to ask about what is on your mind. This feeling is right to lay open and tell the people concerned. Your heart is like a mirror, perfectly clear, like a bright moon hanging in the middle of the sky. The whole poem says: you actually know your own mind. Speak it out and act openly, and things will become clear.
9.overall: This lot says you already have the answer, so there's no need to go around in circles. Saying your thoughts honestly is more useful than hiding them and guessing. Your mind is clean and your intentions are good, so you have nothing to fear from being seen. Now is a good time to lay things out in the open and talk about them. Be upright and you will naturally be understood.
9.love: If you're in a flirtation, your feelings are already obvious, so you might as well say it directly. The other person is probably waiting too. If you've lost contact, send a sincere message saying what you really want to say. If you're hoping to get back together, being frank about what you thought then and what has changed since works better than testing the waters. If you're in a relationship, say what's on your mind instead of bottling it up, and the relationship will be as clear as moonlight. Once it's said plainly, you both feel lighter.
9.work: At work, speak up with your ideas. Talking with your manager or colleagues will bring understanding. If you're job hunting or changing jobs, being honest about your motives in an interview actually helps. In a deal, discuss the terms openly. The more transparent, the smoother.
9.ask_next: You already have the answer in your heart. What would you most like to know: which days are best to speak up?
9.ji: Hiding your feelings and making others guess

10.title: The treasure is at home, no need to look elsewhere
10.plain: Priceless treasures are stored right in your cabinet, yet you keep going off to distant places to search. It is like carrying a lamp to look for fire when the fire is already in your hand. Better to sit quietly and stop wearing out your mind. The whole poem says: what you want is actually right beside you, and chasing it outside is wasted effort.
10.overall: This lot reminds you to stop and look at what you already have. You may have felt the answer was far away or in someone else's hands, and the more you searched, the more tired you got. In fact your resources, abilities and connections are all within reach. Now is a good time to quiet down and take stock. Make good use of what's in front of you first, and don't rush to venture out.
10.love: If you're in a flirtation, you may have been looking at people far away without noticing the one nearby who has always been kind to you. If you've lost contact, don't ask around for news of them. Settle your heart first. If you're hoping to get back together, ask yourself whether you miss that person or who you were back then. If you're in a relationship, your partner's good qualities are right in front of you, so treasure them and stop comparing them with others.
10.work: If you're thinking of changing jobs, first see whether your current position still has room for you to shine. You don't have to jump out. If you're job hunting, starting with people you know and old contacts may work better than sending applications everywhere. A business partner may be right beside you.
10.ask_next: The treasure is within reach. What would you most like to know: which days suit quieting down and sorting things out?
10.yi: Take stock of what you already have

11.title: A busy stretch first, then a helper leads you somewhere good
11.plain: The good thing you seek will bring great joy, though in matters of romance and marriage there may be a short stretch of busyness and confusion. In the end it still turns out well, and a helpful person will take you in and lead you to a good place. The whole poem says: the process will have some twists and bustle, the result is good, and someone will help you.
11.overall: On the whole this lot is a good one, and it only warns that there will be a stretch of confusion in the middle. Don't doubt the result just because the process is a bit messy. During this time, watch for people around you who are willing to help, since they will be the key to lifting you up. Now is a good time to steady your mood and follow your plan, and the good thing will see it through to the end.
11.love: If you're in a flirtation, you may run into small hiccups, like schedules that don't match or messages that come in fits and starts. Don't take them too seriously. If you've lost contact, reaching out through a friend works better than forcing a message yourself. If you're hoping to get back together, there will be some push and pull, but there is a chance of finding your way back. If you're in a relationship, talking about marriage or meeting family will bring a busy stretch. Handle it patiently, and the result is good.
11.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, the process may be tedious, but someone will recommend you and help you. A deal will have some changes along the way, but it can still be settled in the end. Keep in touch with senior people and former colleagues. Be a little patient and don't give up too soon.
11.ask_next: A helper will appear. What would you most like to know: roughly when will you meet them?
11.yi: Follow your plan step by step
11.ji: Doubting the result when it gets messy

12.title: Bad luck runs its course, and good news is coming
12.plain: The time has come. The bad has reached its end and the good is about to arrive. Lift your spirits and walk yourself out of the gloom and dust. If you receive good news at an hour like the Rabbit or Tiger hour, then set your resolve and act, and things will go smoothly. The whole poem says: the low point is almost over, so pick yourself up and seize the good news when it comes.
12.overall: This lot is "the worst has passed, and good times return." The hardest stretch is almost over. Don't stay curled up in the low mood. Shake off the dust and stand up again. The original mentions "Mao and Yin," which means good news has its own timing and doesn't come every day. To learn which days those are, cast a hexagram about this matter.
12.love: If you're in a flirtation, the earlier coolness will slowly warm up. Pull yourself together and offer some goodwill first. If you've lost contact, you may hear from them. When you do, reply warmly and don't put on airs. If you hope to get back together, the low point is passing and there's a chance to talk again, so get yourself in order first. If you're already together, the friction of recent weeks will fade, and the two of you can set a new goal together.
12.work: If you're job seeking or thinking of changing jobs, the low stretch is nearly over and good news may reach you, so update your résumé first. At work, set your direction and put in real effort, and things will go more smoothly. A deal that stalled can be taken up again.
12.ask_next: Good news is coming soon. What do you most want to know: which days it will land on?
12.yi: Pick yourself up and leave the low
12.ji: Staying curled up in the low mood

13.title: A good start, but you still have to earn your name
13.plain: You were born into a well-off family, and everything around you, big and small, is plentiful and refined. Then the poem says that only when you are granted the golden fish pouch, a sign of rank for officials in ancient times, and your name spreads across the land, is there something truly worth boasting about. The whole poem says: your conditions and starting point are good, but real glory comes only when you are recognized for your own work.
13.overall: This lot says the resources in your hands are decent and your circumstances are comfortable. But it puts the weight on being "granted": real achievement is others recognizing your ability, not leaning on your background. Now is a good time to make full use of what you have and go after a position that proves yourself. A good name will follow.
13.love: If you're in a flirtation, good circumstances are a plus, but the other person cares about your sincerity, not show. If you've lost contact, don't try to get attention with material things or bragging. One honest sentence works better. If you hope to get back together, let them see how you've grown, not what you own. If you're already together, beyond living well, give each other recognition and respect. Keep score less and put in more care.
13.work: At work you have good resources and can go for a bigger role or title. If you're job seeking or changing jobs, choose a stage where you'll be noticed. In a deal, letting your ability speak will take you further than relying on connections.
13.ask_next: The time of being recognized will come. What do you most want to know: which days are good for going after it?
13.yi: Use what you have to seek opportunity

14.title: The crane leaves its cage, and every road is open
14.plain: Like an immortal crane flying out of the cage that held it, you throw off everything that bound you, and every way is clear. South, north, east, west, nothing stands in the way. You can rise straight up, all the way to the ninth heaven. The whole poem says: the restraints are loosened, and now you are free to do what you want.
14.overall: This lot means release and freedom to act. The matters that tied you down and the worries that kept you from moving are loosening. Now is a good time to act boldly, and your direction is freer, with no need to be boxed in by old rules. Just remember, as you rise, to keep your goal in sight so you don't scatter.
14.love: If you're in a flirtation, put your worries down and express yourself openly. That's better than hesitating in place. If you've lost contact, it may mean you also need to step out of this attachment and free yourself. If you hope to get back together, ask yourself whether you want to go back or simply can't let go, and decide once you're clear. If you're already together, give each other more space and the relationship will feel lighter. Lighten your own heart first, and the relationship will follow.
14.work: If you want to change jobs, switch fields, or start a business, the timing suits you, so feel free to try. Things that were stuck will loosen and the process will smooth out. In a deal, don't be bound by unreasonable terms. Negotiate what needs negotiating. Settle your direction before you take off.
14.ask_next: The cage is open. What do you most want to know: which days are smoothest for setting out?

15.title: A hard insult to swallow; hold steady and don't move
15.plain: Being offended by someone's words is the hardest thing to swallow. Suddenly trouble and danger come to your door. It's like a bird's egg broken and the nest left empty, with no place even to spend the night. At such a time, keep your heart on one word: steady. The whole poem says: don't clash with someone over a moment's anger. Seek stability first and protect yourself.
15.overall: This lot reminds you that the trouble in front of you most likely begins with a quarrel or conflict. The most important thing now is not to be pushed along by emotion. Bear it for the moment so it doesn't grow. Look after your foundations first, such as your home, income, and body. If it involves a dispute or legal matter, turn to a professional rather than carrying it alone.
15.love: If you're in a flirtation and one remark left you uncomfortable, don't snap back right away. Calm down first, then speak. If you've lost contact, an earlier quarrel may be the cause, and this isn't the time to dig up old accounts. If you hope to get back together, set your feelings down first, or meeting will only lead to another fight. If you're already together, be careful that sharp words don't hurt the bond. Say what you need to say gently and protect your home first. Talk once the anger has passed.
15.work: At work it's easy to clash with people, so leave room in what you say and don't turn on someone on the spot. If you're job seeking or changing jobs, don't quit on impulse. Leave only once you're sure of your next step. If a deal is in dispute, ask a professional for help.
15.ask_next: Steady your heart first. What do you most want to know: when will the storm pass?
15.ji: Locking horns over a single remark

16.title: The furrowed brow eases, and jade in the mud is seen
16.plain: The worries that made you frown and turn everything over are loosening for now. The clouds are parting right before your eyes and the sun is out. You are like a piece of jade buried in mud, waiting for a skilled craftsman to lift you out of the dust. The whole poem says: your worth has always been there, just not yet seen, and someone who knows value is about to appear.
16.overall: This lot says your worries are about to ease and a turning point is close. You do have value, but your surroundings have buried it. There's no need to rush to prove anything now. Keep your skills in good shape and wait for the person who understands you. When the opportunity comes, receive it openly, and don't think less of yourself first.
16.love: If you're in a flirtation, the other person may be slowly seeing your good qualities, so don't give up in a hurry. If you've lost contact, your worries will lighten, so reach out once you feel better. If you hope to get back together, letting them see who you've become after settling is more useful than explaining over and over. If you're single, someone who understands you will appear. If you're already together, the sulking of recent weeks will clear, so affirm each other more. Let the good feeling return slowly.
16.work: If you're job seeking or changing jobs, you'll meet someone who appreciates you, so keep your résumé and work samples updated. At work, effort that was overlooked may finally be noticed. In a deal, finding a partner who understands your worth matters more than finding the one with the best terms.
16.ask_next: Someone who knows value is about to appear. What do you most want to know: roughly when you'll meet them?
16.yi: Receive the opportunity openly when it comes

17.title: Ignore idle talk and quiet your mind
17.plain: Don't listen to idle talk and gossip. Morning and evening, just quiet your mind and recite "Amitabha," so your heart settles and focuses. If you take what others say carelessly as true, it's like drawing a cake on paper: how could it fill your stomach? The whole poem says: don't be led along by rumors. Steady your heart, because only what is real counts.
17.overall: This lot reminds you there is a lot of noise around you now, and some words sound true but are empty. Don't be led along by rumors, promises, or gossip. Give yourself a little quiet time each day to gather your mind back, and judge by what actually happens, not by what you hear.
17.love: If you're in a flirtation, the other person may talk sweetly, but watch what they do. Don't live on sweet words alone. If you've lost contact, don't let secondhand news from friends send your mind spinning. If you hope to get back together, see whether their promises can be kept. If you're already together, don't let outsiders' gossip affect you two. If you have doubts, ask them directly and listen to what they say, which is more reliable than hearing it from others.
17.work: At work, stay out of gossip and quarrels and focus on doing the job well. If you're job seeking or changing jobs, get the terms offered in writing and don't rely on spoken words alone. In a deal, look at the actual contract and results.
17.ask_next: Now that your mind is quiet, what do you most want to know: which days suit making a decision?

18.title: Sun and moon take their turns, and every trade goes smoothly
18.plain: The sun sinks in the west and the moon rises in the east. Day and night take turns, as they have since ancient times. A person on a spiritual path who draws this lot finds nothing out of place. Workers, merchants, farmers and students are each content in their own way. The whole poem says: things move at their natural rhythm, and when each person keeps to their own part, all ends well.
18.overall: This lot is steady and smooth. It speaks of pattern and rhythm. The sun sets, the moon rises, and everything follows its proper order. There is no need to rush, and no need to be afraid. Now is a good time to work at your own pace: rest when it's time to rest, act when it's time to act. Whatever your line of work, keeping to your part will bring a return.
18.love: If you're in a flirtation, the feeling is developing at its natural rhythm, so don't try to speed it up. If you've lost contact, it can be like sun and moon taking turns: messages will go back and forth, so feel free to send a light one. If you hope to get back together, it's easier to talk once you're both in step. If you're in a relationship, a steady, regular life is the best state to be in, so enjoy the everyday together. There is sweetness in the plain days too.
18.work: Whatever your line of work, things look fairly smooth for now. Just keep to your pace. If you're job hunting or thinking of changing jobs, going step by step will bring results. Cooperation runs smoothly when each side does its own part well. Work steadily, and the gains will build up little by little.
18.ask_next: The days are running smoothly. What do you most want to know: which days are best to make your move?

19.title: Wind and waves are high; wait for calm before sailing
19.plain: You push a boat out onto a river shoal where the current runs fast, and a wild wind whips up big waves. What can you do about it? Wait until the waves settle and the wind drops, then bring the boat back steadily, and there will be no danger. The whole poem says: the wind and waves are high right now, so don't force your way out. Wait for things to calm down before you act, and you will be safe.
19.overall: This lot is about waiting when the timing is wrong. The situation in front of you is chaotic, and acting now carries high risk. This isn't telling you to give up. It's telling you to wait for the waves to settle. Look after your boat and think your plan through. When things have steadied, set out, and you'll go steadily and safely.
19.love: If you're in a flirtation, the other person's mood or life is in disorder right now. Don't rush to confess; wait until they've settled. If you've lost contact, a message now could easily be misunderstood, so wait for the storm to pass. If you hope to get back together, you're both still angry, so give it a calm stretch first. If you're in a relationship and have been arguing lately, pause, and talk properly once emotions have eased. Words only get through when the mind is quiet.

40.title: Sun sets, moon rises: walk to a different rhythm

41.title: Don't mistake the sweetness in front of you for a good thing
41.plain: There are many good things, and you need to remember which ones are truly good. Your situation is like mistaking a thief for your own child, or raising something that will hurt you as if it were a treasure. Don't be greedy for the small sweetness in front of you. 42.title: Benefits shared by all, everyone looked after
42.plain: You scatter your kindness and care like rain, nourishing without limit. When you pray and make wishes, you favor no side. Everyone with feeling and life receives some benefit. 44.title: Evenly matched at the board, keep your next move hidden
44.plain: When you play against an opponent of equal strength, keep your thoughts hidden. Black and white stones are still locked in struggle on the board, and the outcome isn't settled. 45.plain: Gentleness and softness naturally overcome rigid force. When a family builds up good deeds, its blessings grow abundant. 56.title: A small stream full of rocks: heading to the big river makes it smooth
56.plain: The mountain gully is small and the rocks are rough, and the water rushes past with a roar. Struggling to pole a boat here, you may get hurt. Find a way to guide the boat out to the big river ahead. Once the wind is still and the tide is level, any way you go will be fine. The whole poem says: where you are now is too narrow and rough, and forcing it will hurt you. Find a way out first, and when conditions settle, you'll be fine.
56.overall: This temple lot is about not forcing it in a narrow place. Your current conditions are poor, and the harder you push, the easier it is to get hurt. First find a way to steer toward a wider place: change the setting, change your approach. When the outer storm calms, things can go along smoothly, with no need to force them.
56.love: If you're in a flirtation, things between you are a bit bumpy right now. Don't rush to move forward, and first find a relaxed way to be together. If you've lost contact, don't force contact while emotions are still high. Wait until you both calm down. If you hope to get back together, first work out a new way of being together, and don't circle back into the old problems. If you're in a relationship, there has been a lot of small friction lately. Changing the setting or the pace will help a lot.
56.work: If you're job hunting or thinking of changing jobs, your current position is too narrow and the resistance is great, so you can start looking for a bigger stage. Don't force the plan in your hands yet. Wait until conditions are ripe. If you're negotiating a deal, settle the direction first, then talk details.
56.ask_next: The storm will calm. What do you most want to know: which days are good for setting the boat out?
56.ji: Forcing it in a narrow place and not leaving

57.title: Let gossip blow past like the wind: your days are bright
57.plain: When you hear others saying this and that, let it pass by your ear like the wind. Good food, good clothing, and good income are like the sun hanging in the sky, clear and bright. Remember what will happen later: by then, your heart will feel just as I say now. The whole poem says: ignore the gossip and keep your heart on your own road, and time will prove these words.
57.overall: This lot urges you not to listen to gossip. There may be rumors or criticism around you, but they are only wind, so don't take them to heart. Your foundation is sound, and this is your time to shine. Put your energy into your own goals, and looking back later, you will see that the choice you make now was the right one.
57.love: If you're in a flirtation, don't let your friends' comments sway you. Your own feelings matter most. If you've lost contact, don't rely on what others say the other person thinks. If you have questions, face them directly. If you hope to get back together, set other people's opinions aside for now and ask yourself what you truly want. If you're in a relationship, don't bring outsiders' gossip home to fight about. Two people who are on the same page matter more than anything.
57.work: If you're job hunting or thinking of changing jobs, don't be scared off by online reviews. Go and find out for yourself. When rumors circulate at work, don't respond. Just do your work well. If you're negotiating a deal, when both sides are on the same page, the collaboration will go smoothly.
57.ask_next: Once your hearts are aligned, what would you most like to know: which days suit settling things in words?
57.yi: Keep your mind on your own path

58.title: Stay with your own trade; don't search elsewhere
58.plain: Take to heart the words of those who are loyal and kind. Don't go off to another place to learn a different craft. The poem urges you to stay calmly with your original work and life. Apart from holding on to what you have and letting it slowly grow into surplus, the other paths are not quite right. The whole poem says: your original path is the right one, so rather than switching tracks, go deeper and do better with what you already have in hand.
58.overall: This lot urges you to stay with your own work. Don't rush to change careers or start something new right now. Opportunities that look better from the outside aren't necessarily right for you. Listen to those who truly wish you well. If you tend your existing skills and position with care, you can live comfortably.
58.love: If you're in a flirtation, don't flirt with one person while looking at others. If you focus, they will feel it. If you've lost contact, don't rush to find someone new to fill the gap. First think clearly about who you really care about. If you hope to get back together and the old bond still has a foundation, tending it well is steadier than starting over. If you're in a relationship, cherish the person beside you and listen to the honest words they give you.
58.work: If you're job hunting, looking in a field you know well works best. If you're thinking of changing jobs or careers, hold off for now and go deeper in your current line. If you're negotiating a deal, look for old partners you know and trust.
58.ask_next: Once you've held to your own trade, what would you most like to know: when is a good time to take a step forward?
58.yi: Do what's in your hands deeply and well
58.ji: Rushing to switch tracks and start over

59.title: Climbing high to hide, surrounded by thorns
59.plain: You climb straight up a tall building to hide, never expecting to find thorns and weeds all around. Who knew the arrangement behind the scenes was already set, and the one who was pleased with himself became the one who lost heart. The whole poem says: trying to avoid a problem by hiding or standing high may not work, and your situation can turn over, so see your surroundings clearly before you act.
59.overall: This lot reminds you that avoiding things is no solution, and that you shouldn't relax too much when things go well. What you want to hide from now will follow you wherever you go, and there are plenty of obstacles around you. Rather than keep retreating, face it head on and clear the troubles near you one by one. Stay modest when things go smoothly, so you don't fall suddenly.
59.love: If you're in a flirtation, don't hide and stop responding for fear of getting hurt. When it's time to state your position, state it. If you've lost contact, hiding won't make the problem go away. Look for a chance to talk it through. If you hope to get back together, first see what thorns remain between you. If you get together without dealing with them, you will still get hurt. If you're in a relationship, put in effort even when things are smooth, and don't take the other person's kindness for granted.
59.work: If you're job hunting or thinking of changing jobs, don't jump around carelessly just to escape your situation. The new place isn't necessarily better. If you're employed, stay low-key when you're performing well. If you're negotiating a deal, there are many risks around, so read the terms one by one.
59.ask_next: Once you see your surroundings clearly, what would you most like to know: which days suit facing it head on?
59.yi: Deal with the troubles near you head on
59.ji: Hiding from the problem to be done with it

60.title: Carrying firewood to fight a fire: stop first, then tidy up
60.plain: Carrying firewood to put out a fire only makes it burn stronger, with thicker and thicker smoke, until it spreads over a wide area. If you're asking about running a business, planning something, or coming and going, it's better to put things away first, stop fanning that fire, and don't be anxious over it. The whole poem says: using the wrong method on a problem makes it grow, so it's best to stop and tidy up now, and not add fuel to the fire.
60.overall: This lot reminds you that some actions look like solving the problem but are really adding firewood. Don't rush to patch things up now, because patching makes it worse. Stop first, wrap up what's in your hands, and keep the loss from growing. Calm down and see where the fire started, then decide your next step. That helps more than rushing around anxiously.
60.love: If you're in a flirtation, the more you try to prove yourself, the more you may push the other person away. Pause first. If you've lost contact, don't send several messages in a row when emotions run high. It will only make things stiffer. If you hope to get back together, arguing or chasing right now is adding firewood, so let you both cool down first. If you're in a relationship, stop when you argue. Don't bring up old grievances or say harsh words. Talk once the anger has passed.
60.work: If you're job hunting or thinking of changing jobs, don't quit on impulse or make big decisions for now. If you're negotiating a deal, investing, or expanding, pause and don't sink deeper. For anything that's gone wrong, cut your losses and tidy up first.
60.ask_next: Once the fire has stopped, what would you most like to know: when is a good time to start again?
60.yi: Stop first and wrap things up
60.ji: Rushing to fix it and making it worse

61.title: A lively gathering, but the heart can't stay hidden
61.plain: Reciting poems by day, singing by night, joining in the fun wherever the occasion calls, laughing happily. But when everyone actually meets face to face, what's in the heart is hard to hide. In the end there is a chorus of cheers, and everyone hums a little tune together. The whole poem says: days are lively and look carefree, but when people gather, true feelings and the real story show, so see clearly what is show and what is real.
61.overall: This lot has a lively mood, with good social standing and a good scene, but it reminds you to tell playing along from being sincere. You can go to social events and gatherings and let them open up your relationships. Just don't treat polite words as promises, and don't assume no one can read what's on your mind. Say what needs to be said early, which is better than being seen through on the spot.
61.love: If you're in a flirtation, enjoying a chat doesn't mean they're serious. Watching how they treat you in a crowd is more reliable than sweet words in private messages. If you've lost contact, you may run into each other at a gathering or among mutual friends. Be natural then, and don't deliberately avoid them. If you hope to get back together, a heart that still cares can't be hidden. Rather than pretend nothing is wrong, honestly say a word. If you're in a relationship, don't let jokes and social obligations turn into misunderstandings. Let your partner know what they should know.
61.work: If you're job hunting, go to more gatherings and networking events, since opportunities often pop up there. If you're changing jobs, don't be drawn in by surface liveliness. Ask clearly what the actual work is. If you're negotiating a deal, terms agreed over a meal only count once they are put in writing afterward.
61.ask_next: Lively as the scene is, what would you most like to know: which days suit saying what's truly in your heart?
61.yi: Say what needs to be said early

62.title: With support in your heart, danger can be passed
62.plain: The poem says morning and night you are held up by the Buddha. You can read this as: with something to rely on in your heart and kind thoughts kept each day, a person stays steady. So even if you meet danger, you won't truly sink into it. If a helpful person then comes to give you a hand, good fortune and gains will follow on their own. The whole poem says: with a calm heart and someone to guide you, hard-looking passes are crossed one after another.
62.overall: This lot says that although there is some risk before you, it won't lead to anything serious. The key is whether your heart stays steady. Do what you need to do each day, keep kind thoughts, and don't panic when things happen. Next, pay attention to people around you who are willing to help. Ask for advice and accept introductions, and things will go smoothly thanks to one person's help.
62.love: If you're in a flirtation, the relationship may look a bit precarious, but it isn't that dangerous. Keep your own pace, and the other person will sense your sincerity. If you've lost contact, you can reconnect through a mutual friend, a kind of helpful person, instead of forcing your way in. If you hope to get back together, settle your heart first, and don't send messages when your emotions are most tangled. If you're in a relationship, don't panic when friction comes. Talk with an elder or friend you trust, and often a single sentence clears it up.
62.work: If you're job hunting or thinking of changing jobs, things are somewhat uncertain now but won't reach a dead end. Ask seniors for advice and ask people to recommend you, and opportunities will be brought in. If you're negotiating a deal, an intermediary making the introduction will help things go more smoothly. Move forward once the terms are settled.
62.ask_next: A helpful person will appear. What would you most like to know: roughly which days make it easier to meet them?
62.yi: Ask for advice and accept introductions

63.title: Needle in the ocean: even if you find it, it takes great effort
63.plain: You dropped a needle into the sea once, while traveling by boat, and today you are still searching the water for it. Even if you do find that very needle, you will have spent a lot of effort and a lot of heart. The whole poem says this: getting back something you lost in the past is not impossible, but the cost is high, so think first about whether it is worth it.
63.overall: This lot asks, "Is it worth it?" What you are chasing may be something from the past, a missed chance, or an old relationship. It is not hopeless, but it will take more time and energy than you expect. Work out how much you are willing to give, then decide whether to keep searching or put your strength somewhere new.
63.love: If you are in a flirtation: trying to bring back a feeling that has gone cold will be tiring, so see whether the other person responds before you put in more. If you have lost contact: you can reach them, but it will take a lot of patience, so don't expect to return to how things were in one go. If you hope to get back together: this lot speaks to you most. An old love can be found again, but it takes effort and heart, so ask yourself whether you want this person or just can't accept the loss. If you are in a relationship: to find the early warmth again, you both need to spend time on it together.
63.work: If you want to return to an old company or field, or recover an old debt or old client, you can try, but it will cost time and energy. If you are job hunting, rather than keep staring at the one opening you missed, apply to several new ones at the same time. In a deal, if an old partnership restarts, renegotiate the terms.
63.ask_next: Finding it back will take effort. What do you most want to know: which days are more likely to bring a clue?
63.yi: Work out first whether it is worth it
63.ji: Chasing the past at any cost

64.title: A fish in the net: don't thrash around yet
64.plain: Like a golden fish put back into clear, rippling water, you think you are free, but out of sight a net has closed in on every side. You think and think and find no way to turn and get out. You have reached the deepest pass, suffering alone, sad alone. The whole poem says this: a situation that looks smooth may hide limits you haven't noticed, and when you are trapped, don't tough it out alone.
64.overall: This lot is a reminder, not a verdict. You may feel tied down by many conditions right now, and every move seems wrong. The more you thrash, the tighter the net pulls. Stop first and look at what is holding you, one thing at a time. Find someone you trust to think it through with you, and don't swallow all the hardship yourself. When you can't get out, keep steady first, and move once you see clearly.
64.love: If you are in a flirtation: this relationship may be more complicated than you think, and the other person may have ties you don't know about, so don't invest too deeply yet. If you have lost contact: they may be caught in their own situation, not unwilling to answer you. If you hope to get back together: pulling them back by force now could leave you both stuck, so take care of yourself first. If you are in a relationship: if you feel you can't breathe, say how you feel instead of grieving alone in silence.
64.work: Your current job may have limits you can't see, such as contract terms or office politics. If you are job hunting or changing jobs, read the conditions and contract details carefully first. In a deal, confirm the other side's background and who is responsible for what. Better to go slower than to sign and find out you are tied down.
64.ask_next: For now, keep steady. What do you most want to know: when is the net more likely to loosen?
64.yi: Find someone you trust to think it through with

65.title: Don't cut yourself for a good that's right in front of you
65.plain: What looks cheerful right now may not really be worth cheering for. It seems dangerous, yet not quite dangerous; it seems safe, yet not quite safe. Why cut away good flesh and make a wound? Better to keep things as they were, which is safer. The whole poem says this: don't take needless risks for a passing benefit; keeping things as they are is steadier.
65.overall: This lot advises you not to move yet. A tempting opportunity or change is in front of you, but its risks are unclear. Sacrificing what you have now for it would most likely be wounding yourself. This is a time to hold on to what is in your hands and tend to things as they are. If you want change, ask about the price first. There is no hurry.
65.love: If you are in a flirtation: the other person's sweetness is tempting, but don't give up your own life and friends for them, and see first whether they care about you just as much. If you have lost contact: don't do anything that shortchanges yourself just to reconnect. If you hope to get back together: ask yourself whether you want to return because it was truly good, or because you are lonely for the moment. If you are in a relationship: don't risk it for the thrill of something new outside; holding on to what you have is more grounded.
65.work: If someone invites you to switch jobs or fields, or offers terms that sound great, don't rush to say yes. See the risks clearly. If your current job is tolerable, stay steady for now. In a deal, don't give up too much just to win the order. Hold your bottom line.
65.ask_next: For now, hold on. What do you most want to know: when would it be steadier to consider a change again?
65.yi: Hold on to what you have
65.ji: Risking it for a passing gain

66.title: The road is dangerous and the waves are high: find a place to pause
66.plain: The road is treacherous, and the horse is still walking, but your companions have already gone far ahead. A sheep that left the flock is trapped, just as a tiger appears. A boat must cross dangerous shallows, and then wind rises and waves overturn. Spring is nearly over, the flowers have already fallen, and frost comes down from the sky. All four lines say the same: things go wrong one after another, you are alone and easily meet trouble, and you need to be especially careful.
66.overall: This lot lays out the difficulties all at once so you can prepare early. This is not a time to go it alone, or to rush ahead and take risks. Return to people first and find partners you can lean on. Put off any decision that can wait. The poem's "late spring" means the timing has slightly passed, not that it will always be so. To learn which days are more likely to ease, you can cast a hexagram about it.
66.love: If you are in a flirtation: the other person may already have gone far in another direction, so don't chase too hard alone. If you have lost contact: forcing contact now is likely to hit a wall, so first have friends around you. If you hope to get back together: the timing has somewhat passed, so rather than force it, look after yourself first. If you are in a relationship: when outside pressure is heavy, stand together even more, and don't blame each other in the storm.
66.work: If you are job hunting or changing jobs: there is a lot of competition and uncertainty now, so don't quit without a plan, and don't rush in alone. Keep in touch with people in your field. In a deal, the other side's terms may hide a pitfall, so look carefully first. In your current work, aim first to avoid mistakes.
66.ask_next: Storms always pass. What do you most want to know: which days are better for setting out again?
66.yi: Return to people and find partners

67.title: An upright heart can be weighed fairly
67.plain: A golden scale weighs your heart, no more and no less, neither light nor heavy. Because you are upright in how you treat people, even if you don't understand great writings, you see right and wrong clearly. The whole poem says this: you will be measured by how you treat others; with an upright heart, matters naturally become fair and clear.
67.overall: This lot says you stand on firm ground. What you give and who you are will be seen clearly, so you needn't worry about being wronged. Handle things now with honesty and fairness. You don't need to copy others' tricks, or dress yourself up as more impressive. Act by your conscience, and the outcome will do right by you.
67.love: If you are in a flirtation: the other person can see your sincerity, so no testing or playing hard to get is needed. Just be direct and genuine. If you have lost contact: you needn't hurry to apologize for what you didn't do wrong. A calm hello is enough. If you hope to get back together: lay out the old problems fairly, without blaming only yourself or only them. If you are in a relationship: what you each give should be balanced, and if it isn't, say so, and the relationship will be steadier.
67.work: If you are job hunting or interviewing: no need to exaggerate. Telling the truth actually helps. If you are changing jobs, choose a place that values fairness and rules. In a deal, state the terms clearly and settle the accounts clearly, so both sides feel at ease and the partnership lasts.
67.ask_next: Fairness will be seen. What do you most want to know: which days suit laying things out and talking openly?
67.ji: Using tricks and dressing yourself up

68.title: The home is clear and bright, good things arrive one by one
68.plain: Inside and outside the house it is clean and bright, and even your dreams are good omens. The goodness your family has built up over time brings prosperity. Disputes can be argued out reasonably, a marriage proposal can be settled, the silkworms are raised and bring a harvest, and a sick person meets the right medicine and slowly recovers. The whole poem says this: do good in ordinary times and take care of your home, and things will move in a good direction in every way.
68.overall: This lot has a calm, favorable feel, and its focus is on "building up goodness" and "caring for home." How you usually treat people and handle things is slowly paying you back now. It suits dealing with matters that have dragged on and putting in order the relationships at home and around you. The poem mentions lawsuits and illness; it means that things can be reasoned through and the right method found. If you really face them, please leave them to professionals such as lawyers and doctors.
68.love: If you're in a flirtation, this lot mentions marriage coming together, so there is room for things to move forward. Let them get to know your life, your family and your friends. If you've lost contact, a misunderstanding can be talked through, so reach out when things are calm. If you hope to get back together, explain the old quarrel with reason, and don't dig up old grievances. If you're already together, it's a good time to talk about the future, meet family, or plan something longer-term.
68.work: If you're job hunting or thinking of changing jobs, the reputation and connections you've built over time are working for you. You can ask former coworkers or managers to recommend you. If a partnership has a dispute, sitting down and talking it through can get results. Bring in a professional if you need to. The work in your hands will bear fruit.
68.ask_next: Good things are coming one by one. What do you most want to know: which days suit settling an important matter?
68.yi: Clear away what you've been putting off
68.ji: Leaving the people close to you neglected

69.title: A plum blossom in winter cold blooms again when spring comes
69.plain: Winter has come, and there is a single plum branch on the mountain ridge. The leaves have all fallen and the branch looks dried out, yet it never breaks. Word is that warm spring is almost here, and when it comes, the plum will still bloom as the finest flower of all. The whole poem says: you are in winter now, and things look bare, but the roots are still there. When the time comes, you will stand again in your rightful place.
69.overall: This lot goes from cold to warm. Right now things may feel quiet, and you may feel overlooked, but your strength has not been beaten down. What to do now is hold on and look after your foundations. Don't deny yourself because of a low moment. In the poem, "winter" and "warm spring" stand for a low point and a turning point. To learn which days the turn may fall on, cast a hexagram for this matter.
69.love: If you're in a flirtation, the other person may be a little cool right now. That doesn't mean there's no chance. Keeping your own shine works better than chasing them with questions. If you've lost contact, this silence is like winter. Live your own days well, and reach out when a sign of warmth appears. If you hope to get back together, your place in their heart is still there. It's just not the time yet, so don't rush. If you're already together, a flat stretch is normal, and getting through it will make the relationship richer.
69.work: If you're job hunting or thinking of changing jobs, no reply for now doesn't mean no. Keep building your work and your skills, and when opportunity returns you will be the one who stands out. A plan that was set aside may get seen again later. In a partnership, wait patiently for now.
69.ask_next: News of spring is near. What do you most want to know: which days the warmth may return?
69.yi: Hold on and look after your foundations
69.ji: Denying yourself over a low moment

70.title: Like a bee busy all round, time to change direction
70.plain: Busy every day like a bee, flying here and there, back and forth. But spring is nearly over and the flowers have faded. It looks for nectar and finds none. Now it no longer clings to the old patch of flowers. The whole poem says: if you keep rushing about in the same place and gain nothing, it's because the nourishment there has run out. Let go of the old and look for another direction.
70.overall: This lot reminds you that being busy is not the same as making progress. You may have spent a lot of effort circling a place with nothing left to take. Stop and look at which things are habit and which are truly useful. You don't have to force yourself to stay in the old place. You can start planning a new direction, just don't fly around aimlessly again. In the poem, "late spring" is a figure for time having passed, not a date.
70.love: If you're in a flirtation and you're always the one chasing and finding topics while they barely respond, ask yourself whether it's worth it. If you've lost contact and have reached out several times with no answer, you can pause and put your attention back on yourself. If you hope to get back together, the flowers of that relationship may have faded. Letting go is not failure. If you're already together, don't just stay busy coping with daily life. The two of you need to find new ways of being together.
70.work: If you're job hunting or thinking of changing jobs, sending résumés everywhere has limited effect. Work out what you want first, then apply. If your current job is only busy and no longer helps you grow, you can start planning a change. In a partnership, the old way of working together is no longer enough and needs adjusting.
70.ask_next: The old can be let go. What do you most want to know: when is a good time to fly toward a new direction?
70.yi: Stop and see what is truly useful

71.title: A second chance, and a steadier path
71.plain: Who would have thought that someone who was cherished would meet a forceful, overbearing rival, and a good matter would be thrown into disorder. The poem speaks of a woman who took a second marriage that year, meaning a relationship begun again and a second chance. It is like a bow with two arrows: if the first misses, there is still the second. In the end, riding dragon and horse, you land safely. The whole poem says: being thrown off course midway is nothing to fear, and starting over can bring you to a better place.
71.overall: This lot has trouble in the first half and steadiness in the second. You may have been forced to change plans by outside forces, or your first choice may not have worked out. Don't treat this as failure. A second chance often comes with a clearer sense of what you want. You can start over openly from here, while guarding against forceful, unreasonable people or situations.
71.love: If you're in a flirtation, someone may be pushing in, or something may have interrupted you two, but getting close the second time isn't necessarily worse. If you've lost contact, reaching out again is like shooting the second arrow. This time see the target clearly and say what you feel plainly. If you hope to get back together, or have just parted and want a fresh start, it's a good time to give yourself a new chance. If you're already together, a relationship that has weathered a storm knows better how to live steadily.
71.work: If you're job hunting or thinking of changing jobs, a first setback or being pushed out doesn't mean there's no chance. A second application or a change of field may go more smoothly. If you're negotiating a deal, keep a backup: one bow, two arrows, and don't rest all your hope on one party. If you face a forceful opponent, protect your own rights.
71.ask_next: The second arrow is about to fly. What do you most want to know: which days would go more smoothly for you to act?

72.title: You want the honey, but watch for the stinger
72.plain: You tease the bee because you want its honey, but you risk being stung by the needle in its tail. There seems to be a different road ahead that looks like a shortcut, but a thick patch of thorns lies hidden in it. The whole poem says: benefit and risk come tied together. Don't look only at the sweetness. See the cost first.
72.overall: This lot isn't telling you to do nothing. It asks you to act with your guard up. What you want may come within reach, but you could get bitten back along the way. This is especially true of roads that look easy and skip the rules, which often have trouble behind them. Take the proper road, leave yourself a way back, and know how much you're taking and how much risk you're running.
72.love: If you're in a flirtation, the other person may be charming but also have thorns. Watch how they treat others before deciding how much to invest. If you've lost contact, don't reach out by provoking or playing games, or you may get stung. If you hope to get back together, think clearly about whether going back will bring sweetness or pain. If you're already together, be careful of a third person or temptation outside. A road that looks fresh usually has thorns inside.
72.work: If you're job hunting or thinking of changing jobs, check an especially good offer carefully and ask what is required behind it. If someone suggests a shortcut or a loophole, stay away. If you're negotiating a deal, for a high-profit project, spell out the contract and how risk is shared.
72.ask_next: The sweetness and the risk are both here. What do you most want to know: which days would be safer to act?
72.yi: Take the proper road and keep a way back
72.ji: Taking crooked paths for an easy way

73.title: The spring thunder has sounded, time for you to come out
73.plain: The first thunder of spring sounds and shakes awake the insects sleeping in the earth. They shed the dust from their bodies and crawl out of the old holes in the wall. Suddenly wind and clouds meet at just the right moment, and nature works its change: they become a dragon. The whole poem says: you have lain low for a while, and now a force is calling you awake. Keep pace with the times and you can be transformed.
73.overall: This lot means turning things around and transforming. You may have felt stuck for a long time, and now things are starting to stir, with outside opportunities drawing near. It's a good time to step out of your comfort zone and try a new position or role. The key is to really move once you've woken. In the poem, "spring thunder" stands for waking up. To learn which days it may fall on, cast a hexagram for this matter.
73.love: If you're in a flirtation, a relationship that has been quiet for a while will stir again. You can take the lead a little and let them see a different side of you. If you've lost contact, they may have been moved by something and thought of you again. When a message comes, reply warmly. If you hope to get back together, change something in yourself first, then talk about going back, so they can see it. If you're already together, the relationship may take a big step forward, such as moving in together, getting engaged, or planning a new life together.
73.work: If you're job hunting or thinking of changing jobs, your time of lying low is nearly over. Update your résumé and take the initiative. If you want to change fields or start a business, the time is gradually ripening. In a partnership, you will meet the right person at the right moment and click right away.
73.ask_next: The spring thunder has sounded. What do you most want to know: which days are best to act?
73.ji: Staying curled up in your comfort zone

74.title: You walked into the cage yourself. Stop and think first.
74.plain: A wild crane that was once free grew too lazy to fly and walked into a cage on its own. It wanted to soar like the great roc, but fell into a pit instead. Every direction is blocked, you are worn thin, and your heart is full of regret. The poem says this: part of what traps you is your own choice, and reaching for the sky in one step is more likely to leave you with nothing.
74.overall: This temple lot asks you to check your own decisions. The bind you are in now may be somewhere you walked into for convenience or in a moment of hurry. When every side is stuck, stop forcing a leap into the sky and fill in the pit in front of you first. Regret does not help. Find which choice put you in the cage, and the next step will become clear.
74.love: If you are in a flirtation, don't step into a relationship that makes you uncomfortable just because you don't want to be alone. If you have lost contact, think back to how things got here, and don't rush to send another message, or you may sink deeper. If you hope to get back together, expecting one talk to put everything back where it was can lead to disappointment, so go step by step. If you are in a relationship and feel tied down, say so first, adjust together, and don't keep the resentment inside.
74.work: If you are job hunting or thinking of changing jobs, don't say yes just because of short-term stability or an attractive offer. Look carefully at whether it will tie you down. If you hope to leap to a very high position in one go, lay your foundation first. If you are negotiating a deal, there are obstacles on every side, so stay conservative and don't expand.
74.ask_next: Fill in the pit first. What you most want to know is: when will it be easier to spread your wings?
74.ji: Rushing to leap to the top

75.title: Carrying a tiger past the mountain, and someone steps in to help
75.plain: It is like carrying a tiger past the foot of a mountain. You are on edge, so frightened your nerve nearly breaks, and you feel cold all over. Luckily, in front of the mountain you meet a capable expert who steps in to help, and you manage to stay safe. The poem says this: what you are handling is dangerous and hard to control, but when someone who knows the work lends a hand, the danger can pass.
75.overall: This temple lot is about rescue within danger. You may be dealing with a hot potato where one slip could cause trouble, and the pressure is heavy. Don't push through on your own. Reach out to someone with experience and expertise, and listen to their advice. Getting through safely is a good result. Aim for steady, not for a pretty win.
75.love: If you are in a flirtation, this relationship leaves you both hopeful and afraid. Ask a trusted friend what they see, and don't guess alone. If you have lost contact, don't push while feelings are still raw. Ask a friend who knows you both to help ease things. If you hope to get back together, there are hard problems in the relationship, and if needed you can talk them through with a counselor or other professional. If you are in a relationship and face something big, don't carry it alone. Find help together.
75.work: If the project in your hands is tricky or risky, quickly ask someone senior or a professional to look it over. If you are job hunting or changing jobs and the position looks difficult, ask questions before you accept. If you are negotiating a deal, have an advisor or lawyer read the contract, which can help you avoid danger.
75.ask_next: A capable helper will appear. What you most want to know is: on which days are you more likely to meet the person who can help?
75.ji: Pushing on alone to prove yourself

76.title: Holding steady in the cold pool, then leaping the Dragon Gate
76.plain: Fish and dragons are mixed together, looking much alike and getting along peacefully. You wait patiently in the cold, deep pool, and the matter is not yet done. Without noticing, one day horns grow on your head, and with one leap from Yu Gate (the Dragon Gate) you rise to the heavenly palace. The poem says this: for now you blend into the crowd and go unnoticed, but if you can hold steady, one day you will stand out.
76.overall: This temple lot is about enduring first, then rising. Right now you look no different from everyone else and the matter isn't finished, so it is natural to feel anxious. But this stretch is when your horns are growing and you are building up. Keep your patience and keep sharpening your skills. When the chance comes, you will jump up all at once, and the gap between before and after will be large. Don't rush to prove yourself now.
76.love: If you are in a flirtation, you may be just one of many friends in their eyes for now. Don't rush, and let them slowly notice what makes you different. If you have lost contact, the quiet period is a good time to improve yourself, and when you meet again you will turn heads. If you hope to get back together, the other person isn't responding for now. Wait patiently, and the relationship may suddenly step forward. If you are in a relationship, the plain days are laying a foundation, and something worth celebrating together may come soon.
76.work: If you are job hunting or changing jobs and your résumé disappears without a reply, don't lose heart. Keep building yourself up, and when a chance comes you can turn things around at once. If you are employed, the work you do quietly will eventually be seen, and a promotion is possible. In a deal, wait patiently for the negotiation to ripen.
76.ask_next: The Dragon Gate is just ahead. What you most want to know is: which days are best for making that leap?
76.yi: Stay patient and sharpen your skills

77.title: Don't trust wealth in a dream. Wait for a helper to point the way.
77.plain: Talking about a dream inside a dream, you dream you have struck it rich. As for empty fame outside yourself, don't guess at it or chase it either. The mountains are high and the waters far, news is uncertain, and promises are hard to count on. Only when a helpful person points the way do you suddenly see clearly and laugh. The poem says this: the gains in front of you are mostly imagined, so don't take them as real. The true turning point comes when someone points you in the right direction.
77.overall: This temple lot reminds you to tell dreams from reality. The profits and reputation that sound so fine are still castles in the air, so don't bet big on them. Put a question mark on news from far away and on promises not yet settled. Instead of guessing on your own, ask someone who sees clearly. One sentence from them may wake you up.
77.love: If you are in a flirtation, don't love only in your imagination. Judge the sweet words you hear by actions. If you have lost contact, distance and little news make you guess and get more confused, so learn how they are doing through a friend. If you hope to get back together, don't make going back too romantic. First find out what the other person truly thinks. If you are in a relationship that is long-distance or sees little time together, turn promises into concrete plans. With a word of advice from an elder or friend, the knot is easier to untie.
77.work: If you are job hunting or changing jobs, check carefully any opportunity that sounds like an amazing salary. While you wait for a reply from a faraway company or another city, don't resign first. If you are negotiating a deal, profits promised by word of mouth don't count. Ask a knowledgeable senior to take a look, and you can often find the real direction.
77.ask_next: One pointer from a helper and things brighten. What you most want to know is: on which days are you more likely to get word?
77.ji: Betting big on gains not yet real

78.title: With one skill in hand, you can go anywhere without fear
78.plain: Pour cold water on white snow and it slowly melts away. Not too cold, not too hot, the temperature is just right. To travel the whole world you need nothing else, only a solid skill kept within you. The poem says this: a mind that is neither cold nor hot, kept in balance, together with one real strength, is what you can rely on most.
78.overall: This temple lot is grounded. It does not speak of luck. It speaks of ability and good measure. Now is a good time to focus on honing one skill to its best, without trying to grab everything. Handle matters neither coldly nor rashly, but warmly and steadily. With real ability, people need you wherever you go, and your path grows wider.
78.love: If you are in a flirtation, a neither-hot-nor-cold pace is just right. Don't cling too much or turn too cold, and let the other person come close at ease. If you have lost contact, put your focus back on your own life and skills first. When you shine, they will notice. If you hope to get back together, let strong emotions cool first. Talking calmly gives you a better chance. If you are in a relationship, it needs just the right warmth. It doesn't have to be grand, and steady time together is the best state.
78.work: If you are job hunting or changing jobs, put your strongest skill first. It works better than a list of ordinary skills. If you want to switch careers, studying a specialty is a good direction. If you are negotiating a deal, let your ability speak, and the other side will see your value.
78.ask_next: You have the skill. What you most want to know is: on which days is it best to show it?
78.ji: Trying to grab everything at once

79.title: Your wish came true. Don't forget the promise you made.
79.plain: You once made a wish to the sky, and with it formed a bond of favor and fate. Now you are safe and things are going smoothly, but what you promised is not yet done. Catching the rabbit and forgetting the snare, then vanishing without a trace, will not do. How can you brush past the vow you made? The poem says this: after you receive help and your wish comes true, remember to go back and keep your promise.
79.overall: This temple lot is about trust and gratitude. Your situation now may have come from other people's help or from a promise you made. Now that things are better, remember to give back and finish what you agreed to do. Owed favors and promises grow heavier the longer you put them off. Settle them well, and the road ahead will feel easier to walk.
79.love: If you're in a flirtation, don't cool off once you've won the other person's good opinion. Let your warmth live up to the way you first reached out. If you've lost contact, think about whether you promised something and never followed through. That may be the knot. If you hope to get back together, keep an old promise first. It does more than a hundred kind words. If you're already together, don't take what the other person gives for granted, and remember what you said at the start.
79.work: If you're job hunting or thinking of changing jobs, remember to thank the people who recommended or introduced you, and let them know how things turned out. If you've taken a new job, don't cut off your old colleagues completely. If you're negotiating a deal, keep the terms you agreed to. Trust is the capital of any long partnership.
79.ask_next: Keep your promises in mind. What would you most like to know: which days suit repaying this favor?

80.title: Focused on practice, suddenly seen
80.plain: Single-minded, you climb the high mountain to train and learn to be an immortal. You never expected that one day the emperor would summon you and give you responsibility. Like a bright, clear sky, light shines on you often, and your aim is to have your name known in every direction.
