The whole poem says: you focus on your own work without seeking attention, and at an unexpected moment you are recognized and your name spreads.
80.overall: This lot is about being seen and promoted. What you've been quietly cultivating may suddenly catch the eye of someone important. Now is a good time to keep focusing and to work openly and honestly. When an opportunity knocks, accept it graciously. Don't turn it down just because you're used to keeping a low profile. Your ambitions can be a little bigger.
80.love: If you're in a flirtation, living your own life with focus may draw the other person closer. When that happens, don't be too shy. If you've lost contact, the calm you've settled into may make the other person notice you again. When word comes, just respond naturally. If you hope to get back together, the other person will see how you've grown. Be sincere and honest. If you're already together, the relationship is open and above board, so let the people around you get to know the two of you.
80.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, an unexpected invitation or offer may come, and it's worth serious thought. If you're employed, the results of your quiet work will be noticed above you, and a promotion or bigger responsibility may be possible. If you're negotiating a deal, once your name is out there, more people will come to you.
80.ask_next: The time of being seen is near. What would you most like to know: which days an opportunity is most likely to knock?
80.yi: Accept the opportunity when it knocks
80.ji: Declining out of habitual low profile

81.title: A tailwind pushes the boat home with its treasure
81.plain: The leaves in front of the courtyard have fallen. It is deep autumn. The traveler hurries along, as if to race home in one breath. Thanks to a gentle push from Heaven, a favorable wind rises and carries a boat full of treasure all the way home. The whole poem says: you are already working hard to get there, and with circumstances lending a hand, the harvest returns smoothly to you.
81.overall: This lot speaks of effort plus a tailwind. You've been running and pushing hard lately, and outside conditions are now starting to cooperate, so you don't have to keep struggling against the wind. It suits wrapping up what's in your hands and bringing the results home, not opening a new front. "Late autumn" in the poem is an image of harvest. To know which days it points to, cast a hexagram for this matter.
81.love: If you're in a flirtation, you've been working to get closer, and now the other side is starting to respond. Go with the mood without pushing too hard. If you've lost contact, the wind is slowly turning your way. You can try a light message first. If you hope to get back together, you're both tired inside and the wish to come home is stronger, so talking well gives a chance to be together again. If you're already together, it's a good time to plan something that settles you down.
81.work: If you're job hunting, the résumés you sent and interviews you attended will bring replies one after another. If you're thinking of changing jobs, you can move while someone is recommending you or an opening comes your way. If you're negotiating a deal, the terms are mostly settled. Now is the time to bring the project in and close it.
81.ask_next: The tailwind is already blowing. What would you most like to know: which days bring things in most smoothly?
81.yi: Wrap up what's in your hands
81.ji: Rushing to open a new front

82.title: A lotus grows in the fire, its root intact
82.plain: A great fire roars up to the sky, and it seems nothing can be kept. Yet a lotus grows even in the flames. Its root is never damaged, and its leaves stay green and fresh. The whole poem says: though things now feel scorching, urgent and heavy with pressure, your true foundation hasn't burned away, and after you get through, you can still grow well.
82.overall: This lot means there is protection within danger. Things may be chaotic and heated now, with noise and pressure all around, but the core is still there and won't be destroyed. For now, protect the foundation: your body, your credibility, and the people you truly care about. Don't let the flames push you into hasty decisions. When the fire dies down, tidy up and grow new leaves.
82.love: If you're in a flirtation, there may be a misunderstanding or outside interference between you. Don't rush to flare up with your emotions. Where there is real feeling, things won't fall apart. If you've lost contact, after a fierce argument the root of the feeling may not be cut. Let you both cool down, then send one sincere sentence. If you hope to get back together, however fiercely you quarreled, if the foundation remains, a fresh start is possible. If you're already together, you're going through a stress test, and carrying it together will make you steadier.
82.work: At work you may be putting out fires, with chaos, deadlines and misunderstandings. If you're job hunting or changing jobs, don't decide when your emotions are at their fullest. If you're negotiating a deal, even if the process gets heated, as long as the core terms hold, the deal can be saved. Steady yourself, then talk.
82.ask_next: The fire is still burning. What would you most like to know: which days will the flames die down?

83.title: The moon is still partial, and will be full by the fifteenth
83.plain: Like the moon on the third, fourth and fifth of the month, half is visible and half is not, still incomplete. Only on the fifteenth, that good night, will moonlight fill every place and everything be round. The whole poem says: your matter has only partly come together. It has taken shape but is not yet whole. That isn't bad, it's just not the time yet, and when the time comes it will naturally be complete.
83.overall: This lot is about still growing. The matter is half done. Don't write off the whole because you see the missing half, and don't rush it to be full right away. Now is a good time to fill in the gaps step by step and wait patiently for it to ripen. The "third" and "fifteenth" in the poem are images of the moon going from partial to full, not specific dates. To know which days it points to, cast a hexagram for this matter.
83.love: If you're in a flirtation, the other person likes you but isn't at the point of commitment. Give it time to round out slowly, and don't push for a declaration. If you've lost contact, you can only see half the picture now. Don't conclude anything yet, and reach out once the other side is clearer. If you hope to get back together, there's a chance but it isn't ripe, so look after your own half first. If you're already together, you're still adjusting to each other, and a bit more patience will make it more complete.
83.work: If you're job hunting, you may have passed one stage and be waiting for the next. Don't give up in a hurry. If you're changing jobs, the terms are half discussed, and the missing parts will fill in slowly. If you're negotiating, the deal has a rough shape but isn't complete. Settle the details one by one, and when the time comes it will come together.
83.ask_next: The moon is growing rounder day by day. What would you most like to know: which days will it come to fullness?
83.yi: Fill in the gaps step by step

84.title: Don't lose your measure in the rush for face
84.plain: In pursuit of reputation and face, you lose your sense of proportion and can't get along with the people around you. Be most careful that in haste you don't turn a small matter into a bad one. It is like being drunk, not knowing which way you're walking, and finally dozing off in a daze in the shade of a green pine. The whole poem warns: don't let empty fame and hurry cloud your head, because once you're flustered it's easy to choose wrongly.
84.overall: This lot is a reminder: the biggest risk now isn't outside, it's being too hurried and too eager to save face. Haste invites mistakes, and fighting for reputation hurts harmony. Stop first and clear your head. Don't decide when your emotions are high or you're in disarray. Mend relationships first. Going slower will actually keep you steadier.
84.love: If you're in a flirtation, don't act cold or tough just to save face. That only pushes you further apart. If you've lost contact, you may have said something harsh on impulse earlier. Calm down first, and don't send messages when emotions are running high. If you hope to get back together, set aside who was right or wrong. Sincerity matters more than winning. If you're already together, small things may spark quarrels lately. When you're busy, watch your tone even more, so a moment of angry words doesn't become a crack.
84.work: At work, it's easy to clash with colleagues over credit and titles, and stepping back is better. If you're job hunting or changing jobs, don't decide in haste when everything is a mess. Get clear on the situation first. If you're negotiating a deal, read the terms in black and white and don't rush to agree.
84.ask_next: For now, seek clarity. What would you most like to know: which days suit making a decision again?

85.title: An old matter returns, and a helper lifts you up
85.plain: The door behind the mountain opens again, and what was once put away comes back to light. In a garden full of treasures, everyone can gather once more. You recite a newly written poem, lightly tipsy, and your mood grows brighter and brighter. Then a helpful person steps forward to guide you and brings you onto the wide road upward. The whole poem says: something you set aside has a chance to begin again, and this time someone helps you climb.
85.overall: This lot is "start again, and someone helps." A plan or relationship you put down or broke off can be taken out and sorted through again. Relax, do the old thing in a new way, and you may find fresh enjoyment in it. People will appear who are willing to give you a hand. Remember to ask, and remember to accept.
85.love: If you're in a flirtation, a conversation you once had and never spelled out may come up again. Feel free to pick it up. If you've lost contact, an old connection has a chance to be rejoined, so you can send a light, easy message first. If you hope to get back together, this lot is friendly to you. The old affection is still there, and a reunion is possible. If you're in a relationship, it's a good time to try something new together to add some fun, and a friend or elder may help you both along.
85.work: If you're job hunting or thinking of changing jobs, old contacts and former colleagues may bring an opportunity, so don't be afraid to reach out again. A project that was put on hold has a chance to restart. If you're negotiating a deal, a helpful person may make an introduction. Ask for advice openly rather than working it out alone.
85.ask_next: An old matter is about to reopen. What do you most want to know: which days a helper is most likely to appear?
85.yi: Take up what you set aside
85.ji: Being too shy to ask for help

86.title: One leap clears the gate, and spring thunder rolls over flat ground
86.plain: Spring has arrived. Flowers bloom in full on the sunlit terrace. Ships sail ten thousand miles, bringing treasure in all the way. It is like the carp leaping over the three tiers of waves at the Dragon Gate (the legendary gate where a carp that leaps becomes a dragon), or like a sudden thunderclap on flat ground that everyone hears. The whole poem says: the time has come, and what you have worked at will break through all at once, and brilliantly.
86.overall: This lot speaks of a breakthrough. What you've been nurturing is reaching the point where you can cross over in one go. It suits boldness: sign up, make your proposal, state your position, and ride this spring momentum. The "spring" in the poem is an image of everything starting to stir, not a particular month. To learn which days it falls on, you can cast a hexagram for this matter.
86.love: If you're in a flirtation, the mood is warm. Gather your courage and say it, and a good response is quite possible. If you've lost contact, one sudden message may break the silence, like thunder on flat ground. If you hope to get back together, a turning point may come that brings you close again. Just seize it. If you're in a relationship, things may take a big step forward, such as meeting family or talking about living together or marriage. You can consider it seriously.
86.work: If you're job hunting, an interview or exam has a chance to go through in one try. Practice what needs practicing, then go. If you're changing jobs, you can aim for a higher position. If you're negotiating a deal or doing business, a big order may be coming, so it suits an active approach.
86.ask_next: The wave has arrived. What do you most want to know: which days are best for making your move and leaping across?
86.yi: Boldly state your position and go for it

87.title: Halfway up the mountain as dusk nears, don't force the climb
87.plain: You have walked to the mountainside, and the sun already rests on the peak, about to set. Ahead are steep, dangerous cliffs you cannot climb yet. You can only look up at the sky and hope someone looks after you, hanging in midair, unable to go up or come down. The whole poem says: the matter is stuck halfway, the day is late and the road is risky, so charging ahead is no answer.
87.overall: This lot speaks of being stuck halfway. You've come a good distance, but what lies ahead is beyond your current ability and time. Don't push on out of pride. Stop somewhere safe first, then consider whether to change routes or find help. The poem's "looking up to heaven" means keeping your heart steady and your attitude humble: do what you can and leave the rest to time.
87.love: If you're in a flirtation, things are halfway and one more step is hard. Don't push. Just keep up comfortable contact. If you've lost contact, chasing now may hit a wall, so look after your own feelings first. If you hope to get back together, the obstacles are still there. Don't rush for a result, and talk with a trusted friend. If you're in a relationship, you may be facing a real-world snag. Stop and talk it over together rather than carrying it alone.
87.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, this hurdle is harder than expected. You can build up your skills first or ask someone for a referral. If a project is stuck halfway, cut your losses and take stock of resources instead of adding more. If you're negotiating, ease off when the terms are too risky.
87.ask_next: Dusk is near. What do you most want to know: when is the right time to climb again?
87.ji: Forcing your way up when stuck

88.title: A wooden tiger looks frightening but does not bite
88.plain: In the mountain forest sits a tiger carved from wood. From afar it looks majestic, and you can't help feeling uneasy. Even if someone tells you "it's nothing," you are still afraid. The feeling is like walking into the middle of a great river, with water on every side and nothing solid beneath you. The whole poem says: what scares you may not be so frightening, but your unease is real and needs tending first.
88.overall: This lot speaks of a false alarm. What worries you is likely frightening only in appearance and can't actually hurt you. The trouble is that your mind keeps hanging in the air, like being mid-river with no shore to reach. First see the matter clearly: look closer and ask questions rather than judging from a distant impression. Once your mind is settled, the road gets easier.
88.love: If you're in a flirtation, the other person may look hard to approach but isn't so fierce. Don't be scared off by a first impression. If you've lost contact, the worst you imagine is mostly you frightening yourself. You can ask a mutual friend and get clear first. If you hope to get back together, their coolness may be only on the surface, but steady yourself first. If you're in a relationship, saying your unease aloud is much better than silently guessing.
88.work: That stern boss or difficult client at work may only look fierce. If you're job hunting, don't be scared off by the job requirements. Apply first. If you're changing jobs or negotiating a deal and feel unsure, ask more and look into it more. Don't decide from imagination.
88.ask_next: The tiger is only wood. What do you most want to know: which days you can put your mind at rest and move forward?

89.title: Fine jade hides in the stone, and someone points it out to you
89.plain: Your comings and goings, your planning and managing, all prosper and go smoothly. A flawless piece of fine jade was hidden inside a stone, and outsiders could not see it. Now you are lucky to meet someone who knows the trade and points the way. You finally find the treasure, your wish comes true, and you are overjoyed. The whole poem says: you already have something good in you that hasn't been seen yet, and now someone will help you dig it out.
89.overall: This lot is good news, and its focus is being seen. Your ability, your work or your ideas already have value, but are still hidden in the stone. Now is a good time to consult experienced people, accept advice, and let others help point out your strengths. If you're willing to listen and adjust, you can bring the treasure out.
89.love: If you're in a flirtation, the other person may not have seen your best side yet. You can ask a friend to introduce you, or show a side you don't usually show. If you've lost contact, passing word through a friend who knows you both may work better than forcing a message yourself. If you hope to get back together, listening to others' advice may show you a way to untie the knot. If you're in a relationship, you'll find something new and good in your partner, and the warmth grows.
89.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, someone will appreciate your ability. You can ask a senior colleague to look over your résumé or recommend you. If you're negotiating a deal or doing business, things go smoothly in both directions, and guidance from an expert will help more. The work you have is worth organizing and presenting well.
89.ask_next: The treasure is about to show itself. What do you most want to know: which days you're most likely to meet the person who will guide you?

90.title: Good news arrives suddenly, and helpers lift you all the way
90.plain: One day, a letter of good news suddenly comes down from on high. A boat loaded with treasure returns, full to the brim. If you ask what your future will achieve, the answer is that helpful people will support you from start to finish. The whole poem says: good news will come suddenly, and all along your way there are people willing to pull you up and help you.
90.overall: This lot speaks of news and support. The news you're waiting for may drop in suddenly one day, and it is good. During this time, elders, bosses and seniors around you are willing to help. Don't be shy: ask for help when you need it, and show what you can do. Seize the chance to be seen, and you'll come away with a full harvest.
90.love: If you're in a flirtation, the other person may suddenly message you and take a step forward. Just receive it. If you've lost contact, news may come from an unexpected place, maybe through a mutual friend. If you hope to get back together, someone is willing to bridge the two of you, so you don't have to hold on alone. If you're already together, family or friends will support you, and it's a good time to plan something longer-term together.
90.work: If you're job hunting, the notice you're waiting for may arrive suddenly, so keep checking your inbox and phone. If you're thinking of changing jobs, a referral will be faster than searching on your own. At work, someone above you may promote you, and a deal has a good chance of coming together with a full harvest.
90.ask_next: News is on its way. What do you most want to know: roughly which days will it arrive?
90.ji: Being so polite you miss a chance

91.title: Unknit your brow; the road is already level
91.plain: Unknit your furrowed brow. A person of talent will be given great responsibility, and someone will recommend you upward. Before you lies a broad road, flat as the palm of a hand. Whatever you set out to do will go as you wish. The whole poem says: stop worrying. Your ability will be seen, and the road ahead is easier than you think.
91.overall: This lot means "set your mind at ease." What you were worried about will actually turn in a good direction. What to do now is let go of the worry and put your energy into using your abilities. Someone will recommend you and give you a stage. The road is level, so there's no need to detour or doubt yourself. Do what your heart tells you.
91.love: If you're in a flirtation, don't keep guessing in silence. The other person likes you, so you can chat more lightly. If you've lost contact, loosen up first. Tension makes people afraid to come close, so send a light message. If you hope to get back together, a furrowed brow doesn't help. When the chance comes, let the other person see how you've changed. If you're already together, the relationship is on level ground, and doing what you both want will go well.
91.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, your ability will be seen, and someone may recommend you for a better position. At work, if you're given a bigger task, go for it. If you're negotiating a deal, the road is smooth, so just follow the plan.
91.ask_next: The road is level. What do you most want to know: which days are best to start moving?
91.yi: Drop the worry and follow your heart

92.title: Business profits, and one try passes the exam
92.plain: Business can bring gain, and things go as you wish. Blessings, pay, and honor all arrive, and money comes in double. If you're asking about promotion or recognition, it's like a scholar going to the exam and coming home as the top scorer. The whole poem says: whether you seek wealth or a step forward, this period is very favorable, and one move has a chance of succeeding.
92.overall: This lot goes smoothly, and the key is "succeed in one move." Both wealth and reputation are favored, so make the moves you need to make and don't hesitate too long. If you want to study, take an exam, or seek a promotion, now is the right time to go for it. Good luck also needs real ability behind it. Do your homework thoroughly and you can get it done in one go.
92.love: If you're in a flirtation, you can confess more openly. There's no need to keep testing the waters, and the other person may well receive it. If you've lost contact, reach out once on your own and the warmth may come back. If you hope to get back together, your sincerity will be seen. Say it clearly once and don't drag it out. If you're already together, with feelings and finances both steady, it's a good time to talk about a bigger step like marriage or buying a home.
92.work: If you're job hunting, you have a chance of passing an interview or exam on the first try. If you want a promotion or a career change, it's best to bring it up now. If you're in business or negotiating a deal, the profit looks good and terms can be agreed, so you can be more proactive.
92.ask_next: The timing is good. What do you most want to know: which days are most favorable to make your move?
92.yi: Act when it's time to act

93.title: The phoenix, soaked by rain, will fly again when the sky clears
93.plain: A luan bird and a phoenix, such beautiful great birds, have feathers weighed down by rain, and even little sparrows dare to look down on them and bully them. But one day the clouds will part and the sky will clear, and they will shake out their feathers and soar again. The whole poem says: for now you're out of favor, looked down on and bullied, but it's only temporary. When conditions improve, you will spread your wings again.
93.overall: This lot speaks of "a temporary setback." Your nature hasn't changed. The circumstances are simply against you, like a bird that can't fly when its feathers are wet. You don't need to argue with those who look down on you. Protect yourself first and let your feathers recover. When the sky clears, you'll naturally return to your former height. To know roughly when the rain will stop, you can cast a hexagram about it.
93.love: If you're in a flirtation, you may feel ignored or outshone. Don't think less of yourself because of it. Take care of yourself first. If you've lost contact, this isn't the time to chase. Wait until your mood and state have returned, then get in touch. If you hope to get back together, you're at a disadvantage right now, and pleading will only hurt more, so let yourself shine again first. If you're already together and going through a low point, don't blame each other. Get through this rain together.
93.work: At work you may be looked down on by coworkers or have your credit taken. Hold back for now and avoid a direct clash. If you're job hunting or changing jobs, a rough patch doesn't mean you lack ability, so keep building your skills. In a deal, hold on to your terms and push for more when the timing improves.
93.ask_next: The rain will always stop. What do you most want to know: when will the sky clear?
93.ji: Arguing with those who look down on you

94.title: Tell people apart, and staying calm costs you nothing
94.plain: Tell the petty from the noble, and see clearly who is wise and who is foolish. When something goes wrong, gossip and quarrels follow. Play the zither only when you meet someone who understands you, someone worth playing a song for. In the end, it's better to settle down and quietly hold your ground, which costs you the least. The whole poem reminds you: lately misunderstandings easily stir up trouble, so see people clearly, speak less, and stay quiet.
94.overall: This lot is a reminder: right now mistakes and quarrels come easily. Not everyone deserves your whole heart, so first tell who is sincere and who is just watching the show. Save your words for those who understand you, and otherwise move less and argue less. Quietly keeping your own pace serves you better than rushing to defend yourself or to act.
94.love: If you're in a flirtation, first see whether the other person is sincere or just testing, and don't rush in with your whole heart. If you've lost contact, there may be a misunderstanding or someone passing on words in between. Don't rush to explain yourself. Calm down first. If you hope to get back together, talk with friends who truly understand the two of you, and don't listen to too much noise. If you're already together, small things may spark quarrels lately, so argue less and offer more quiet company.
94.work: At work, sort out who you can cooperate with and who only stirs up trouble, and keep written records of important matters. If you're job hunting or changing jobs, don't jump in a hurry. Get clear first, then move. In a deal, double-check the details of the terms to avoid mistakes and disputes.
94.ask_next: For now, quiet down. What do you most want to know: which days are better for making a move again?
94.yi: Speak less, stay calm, keep your pace
94.ji: Rushing to defend yourself or to act

95.title: Built up day by day, your reputation rises on its own
95.plain: Career and merit are built up bit by bit, from morning to night. Glory and good things are too many to count. You are told to remember the time of the "fighting golden roosters," when blessings, pay, and reputation will naturally multiply in value. The whole poem says: your efforts keep accumulating, and there will be a key moment when the results all appear at once.
95.overall: This lot speaks of "accumulating until the time comes." There are many good things, but they don't arrive overnight. They are slowly piled up by what you do each morning and evening. Keep going, and watch for that key point. The "golden rooster" in the original is an image of a moment, not a specific date given to you. To know which days it falls on, you can cast a hexagram about it.
95.love: If you're in a flirtation, affection builds day by day. Keep in touch, and the key moment will come. If you've lost contact, don't rush. At the right moment, one message can reopen the conversation. If you hope to get back together, slowly let the other person see how you've changed. When the timing is right, they will see it. If you're already together, the relationship is steady and warming, and it's a good time to save a little and plan something for the future together.
95.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, your everyday work and reputation are gaining value, and good chances will come naturally when the time is right. At work, steady performance makes a promotion or raise promising. If you're negotiating a deal, seize the key moment and don't miss it.
95.ask_next: That key moment is near. What do you most want to know: which days will it fall on?

96.title: A sincere, settled heart lights up on every side
96.plain: A tall pagoda, out of the ordinary, its eight faces clear and bright, shining in every direction. The poem urges you to set your heart straight and sincere, and to keep a respectful attitude. Someone like that is supported from all sides, and good things keep coming near. The whole lot says: your state is just right — as long as your heart is sincere and steady and you stay humble and respectful, good fortune will come from every direction.
96.overall: This lot is bright, and the key is a sincere heart. Right now every side of you can shine; in how you deal with people and work, you can be smooth and fitting in every direction. The original's "bowing in reverence" can be read as keeping a respectful, earnest attitude toward people and things. When your heart is settled and your manner sincere, the people around you will naturally want to help — just go with the flow.
96.love: If you're in a flirtation, a sincere manner moves the other person more than playing games, and they'll feel it. If you've lost contact, send a message with sincerity — no need to dress it up. If you're hoping to get back together, first sincerely look at your own part of the problem; the other person will be more willing to come close again. If you're already together, mutual respect and appreciation will make the relationship whole, and the people around you will wish you well.
96.work: For job seekers and those thinking of changing jobs, your qualifications shine on every side — going into interviews with a sincere attitude adds a lot. You have good rapport at work and suit leading a team or communicating outward. If you're negotiating a deal, a sincere attitude will bring plenty of support.
96.ask_next: Things are bright right now. What you most want to know is: which days are best for putting this out into the world?
96.yi: Stay respectful toward people and things
96.ji: Restless and going through the motions

97.title: Moonlight on the ground you can't pick up
97.plain: In the garden the moonlight shines, tree shadows swaying thin and sparse, and it looks as if fine jade is spread across the ground. A child runs over again and again to pick it up, but no matter how he tries, he can't. The whole lot says: the good thing you see may just be an illusion made by light and shadow — lovely to look at, but your hand closes on nothing.
97.overall: This lot asks you to tell "looks like" apart from "actually is." That very attractive opportunity or promise in front of you may be a shadow cast by moonlight — beautiful but not solid. Don't keep spending effort grabbing at the same thing you can't catch. Pause first, see clearly whether it's real, and save your strength for what's solid.
97.love: If you're in a flirtation, the other person's warmth may just be the mood of the moment — don't rush to treat it as a promise. If you've lost contact, going back again and again to pick up old happy memories may only tire you out more. If you're hoping to get back together, first be clear whether you want this person or the time you imagine you had. If you're already together, a little less fantasy and a little more real time together will make the relationship steadier.
97.work: For job seekers and those thinking of changing jobs, check whether the contract and details of an opportunity that sounds too good are actually real. At work, don't keep pouring effort into the same thing that won't come together. If you're negotiating a deal, verify the big promises the other side is painting first.
97.ask_next: First tell light and shadow apart from solid things. What you most want to know is: when will a real opportunity come?
97.yi: Save your strength for what's solid
97.ji: Chasing again and again what you can't catch

98.title: When you hesitate, beware of flying into the net
98.plain: Doing business, going back and forth handling matters, your heart stays hesitant and undecided. Carry on like this and you may stir up needless worry and gossip. It's like a bird flying along that runs headlong into a net and gets stuck — and of the people watching from the side, how many really understand your situation? The whole lot is a reminder: hesitation and not looking carefully can both drop you into trouble, so see clearly before you move.
98.overall: This lot is a reminder, and the key is "see the trap clearly." Right now decisions are easy to waver on, and in that wavering you're easy to pull into someone else's game. Don't rush to commit, especially with things like money, contracts, and guarantees. If you have doubts, stop and ask someone you trust or a professional — better to go a little slower.
98.love: If you're in a flirtation, you can't make up your mind — don't sink too deep without knowing the other person's situation. If you've lost contact, don't rush back out of a moment's loneliness; first be clear whether you're just returning to the same dead end. If you're hoping to get back together, it's fine that others don't understand your struggle, but you need to see it clearly yourself. If you're already together, speak up when something's bothering you — don't keep it bottled in, and don't let outsiders' gossip affect the two of you.
98.work: For job seekers and those thinking of changing jobs, check carefully into opportunities whose terms seem unusually good. If you're doing business or negotiating a deal, look closely at contracts and money dealings, and have a professional check things over if needed. If you've been hesitating too long over something in hand, list the risks first, then decide.
98.ask_next: First see clearly where the net is. What you most want to know is: when is it right to make your move?
98.yi: When in doubt, stop and ask
98.ji: Wavering and pulled into someone else's game

99.title: Fire reaches the roof, and a rain puts it out
99.plain: Riding along carelessly, whip in hand, it comes. This matter is half danger, half wealth. It's like a house with fire right at the rooftop, about to go up in flames, when heaven sends a rain that washes the disaster clean away. The whole lot says: you may slip into danger through carelessness, but you won't be left with no way out — at the most urgent moment, there will be a turn.
99.overall: This lot speaks of "danger, but with a way out." The benefit and the risk are tied together, and it's because you took it too lightly at first that things caught fire. Now deal with the most urgent blaze first, and don't add more fuel. The turn will come, but you need to stop the loss and steady yourself first — and stop being so casual in what you do next.
99.love: If you're in a flirtation, you may stir up misunderstandings by being too casual — watch what you say a little more. If you've lost contact, things once flared up badly, but after cooling down there's still room to turn around. If you're hoping to get back together, deal with the thing that hurt most first, then talk about the future. If you're already together, a sizable argument may come soon — don't add fuel to the fire; wait for the other person to cool down, and one good talk can put it out.
99.work: At work there may be urgent matters or slip-ups to handle — put out the fire first, then review. For job seekers and those thinking of changing jobs, there's opportunity and risk — don't jump rashly. If you're doing business or investing, it's half wealth and half risk; ask a professional if needed.
99.ask_next: The rain will come. What you most want to know is: which days will the fire be put out?
99.yi: Deal with the most urgent thing first
99.ji: Taking it lightly and going through the motions

100.title: Thinking east and west — better to stop first
100.plain: One moment you think of going east, the next west, and you can't make up your mind. You tell everyone you meet about it, and the more you talk, the muddier it gets and the deeper you sink. You climb the mountain, but the immortal you hoped to see doesn't appear. Better to go home and rest, and for now stop bringing it up. The whole lot says: the direction isn't set yet, and asking everywhere and running everywhere will only make it messier — stop first and let yourself be still.
100.overall: This lot speaks of "stop first." Right now you have too many ideas and ask too many people, and you lose your own judgment. Everywhere you go looking for answers comes up empty because the time isn't right yet. The best thing now is to set it down for a while and return to your own life; once your heart settles, the direction will surface on its own.
100.love: If you're in a flirtation, you're paying attention to several people at once, or running hot and cold with one — first be clear what you want. If you've lost contact, asking friends everywhere and inquiring all around will only make you more confused — pause for a bit. If you're hoping to get back together, pushing hard now may come up empty; better to live your own life well first. If you're already together, don't take the two of you's business to too many people — hearing too many opinions will only lose you.
100.work: For job seekers and those thinking of changing jobs, don't apply in too many directions at once before the direction is set. If a plan in hand hasn't moved for a long time, you can pause it, rest, and look again. If you're negotiating a deal and the other side's attitude is unclear, don't chase.
100.ask_next: Stopping for a bit is fine too. What you most want to know is: when is it right to bring this up again?
100.yi: Set it down for now and let your heart settle
100.ji: Telling everyone you meet about it
